subject: Sturnix onramp roadmap sketch + 21-day evaluation plan
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@sturnix.com>, Oliver Kane <oliver.kane@sturnix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sturnix onramp roadmap sketch + 21-day evaluation plan

Hi Samantha / Oliver —

Great to meet briefly on the call yesterday. As promised, I’m sharing a lightweight onramp roadmap sketch (both doc + slide skeleton) you can use to drive the initial 21-day evaluation. This is intentionally concise: milestones, owners, and clear acceptance criteria so your team can move quickly.

What’s included in the doc:
- Week-by-week milestones (access -> integration -> validation -> acceptance)
- Concrete success criteria (latency & throughput targets, quality gates, security checklist)
- Recommended test harness and data slices for evaluation

Links:
- MAP sketch (editable): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcd-MAP-sketch
- Slide skeleton (to present to stakeholders): https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1xY-map-slate

Attachments (quick stubs): MAP_template_v0.3.pdf (one-pager), sturnix-risk-checklist.xlsx (security/procurement checklist)

Proposed 21-day sprint (high level):
- Day 0–3: Account & network access, baseline model selection, security signoffs
- Day 4–10: Integration (API calls, sample workload), baseline performance runs
- Day 11–17: User validation, edge-case checks, cost estimates and model tuning
- Day 18–21: Acceptance review & next-step plan (Dedicated vs Hosted guidance)

Quick asks:
1) Can you confirm who will own technical integration on your side and who will own procurement?
2) Which of the proposed kickoff slots work for you: Jul 20 10:00 PDT or Jul 21 09:00 PDT?

We’ll have Marissa join to capture acceptance criteria in the doc and Jonas to run a short performance checklist during the baseline run. If it helps I can convert the doc into a mutual action plan format and lock owners in the first sync.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the sprint scheduled.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: MAP_template_v0.3.pdf (attachment stub), sturnix-risk-checklist.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@sturnix.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.inference>
Cc: Oliver Kane <oliver.kane@sturnix.com>, procurement@sturnix.com
Date: 2026-07-19T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sturnix onramp roadmap sketch + 21-day evaluation plan

Avery —

Thanks for the materials and the clear breakdown. A few quick clarifying items from our side before we lock the kickoff: 

1) Acceptance criteria: can you add a simple accuracy metric example (we’re focused on intent extraction for support routing — target precision >= 92% on our production slice)?
2) Data privacy: we will need to confirm the MAP references our data retention needs and whether test logs stay within our VPC for private deployment.
3) SLA during the eval: can you confirm typical latency SLOs for a 2k token window on hosted vs dedicated?

Procurement looped in. Oliver will handle technical coordination (I’m the product sponsor). I’m available Jul 20 morning PT or Jul 21 late morning — both look possible.

Appreciate it,
Samantha Liu
Head of Product, Sturnix
samantha.liu@sturnix.com

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, procurement@sturnix.com
Date: 2026-07-19T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sturnix onramp roadmap sketch + 21-day evaluation plan

Samantha — thanks, great questions. Answers below and I’ve updated the shared doc with an explicit accuracy gate example and a short privacy note. See the GDoc for inline comments.

> Acceptance criteria: can you add a simple accuracy metric example (we’re focused on intent extraction for support routing — target precision >= 92% on our production slice)?
- Done. I added an \"Intent extraction\" acceptance gate: precision >= 92% on your labelled slice OR F1 >= 0.86 if you prefer a combined measure. We can run the evaluation against the same sampling you use in prod.

> Data privacy: we will need to confirm the MAP references our data retention needs and whether test logs stay within our VPC for private deployment.
- Noted. The MAP includes a short privacy section. For Hosted evaluation we can enable a private ingestion path and ensure logs are purged after X days; if you require, we’ll set up a Private deployment (VPC) for the sprint — Marissa can add the KMS/HSM integration notes.

> SLA during the eval: can you confirm typical latency SLOs for a 2k token window on hosted vs dedicated?
- Typical baselines we see: Hosted: p95 ~ 320–450ms for 2k tokens on our verified medium models (depends on model family); Dedicated (reserved GPU): p95 ~ 120–250ms depending on instance size and quantization. Jonas will own the baseline run and share a short perf checklist in the GDoc so we can capture exact numbers for your workload.

I also added a proposed owner column in the MAP doc:
- Sturnix: Technical owner = Oliver Kane, Procurement = procurement@sturnix.com
- Redwood: Integration lead = Jonas Weber, Security/Compliance = Marissa Cole

Proposed kickoff: Jul 20 10:00 PDT — please confirm and I’ll send a calendar invite. If that doesn’t work, Jul 21 09:00 PDT is our backup.

Next steps for us internally: Marissa will seed the acceptance criteria table and I’ll lock owners in the MAP. Jonas will prepare a short perf runbook (script + sample workload) we can run on Day 5.

Thanks — sending updated links shortly.

Best,
Avery

Avery / Samantha —

Quick note from my side: I reviewed the MAP sketch and added two items to the slides: (1) explicit data retention bullets for the eval (we recommend 14 day logs purge unless you require longer), and (2) an acceptance matrix example (Intent precision, p95 latency, error-rate on edge cases). I put comments where we’ll need procurement signoff language and flagged the KMS flow for private deployment.

Jonas will bring the perf runbook on the kickoff — he’s pulling a short script that runs the sample slice (non-prod keys) and produces the baseline numbers. I’ll also share a short compliance stub (SOC2 checklist + evidence artifacts) in the MAP doc for your procurement team.

Confirming Jul 20 10:00 PDT works for me — sending a quick invite now.

Marissa Cole
